html:
The Mingin were an Aboriginal Australian people of the country near the southern shore of the Gulf of Carpentaria, around today's Burketown in Queensland. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Little is recorded of them beyond their name and territory. Their land is low coastal plain, salt flats and river mouths. Neighbours on the map include the Kukatj, the Ganggalida and the Nguburinji. Burketown was founded in the 1860s as cattle stations spread over the Gulf country. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
